questions.question: What is the first operating scope: one parish, one archdiocese with several parishes, or several independent dioceses? Name the intended first setting.
Which three problems must the first release solve well enough that parishes will use it regularly?
Who is the primary daily user, and what are that person's five most frequent tasks today?
Which other users must be served at launch, and how often will each use the system?
For every module in the project-review inventory, choose first release, later, or remove. Which existing modules are essential to keep exactly as they operate now?
Which real procedures must remain on paper or happen in person, even when the system records their progress?
Which church rites, ecclesiastical structures and sacramental practices must launch support? Which visible options should be excluded?
Where and on what devices will people work: parish-office computers, shared desktops, personal phones, tablets at events, or elsewhere?
What languages must be complete at launch for the interface, user content and official documents separately?
Who has final authority to approve product design, parish-office workflow, clergy rules, financial controls and sensitive-data access? Assign each area an owner.
What operating scale must the design accommodate: parishes, people per parish, staff, active requests, simultaneous event check-ins and historic records?
What concrete outcomes will establish that the UI/UX is ready for implementation, and which representative users will validate them?
Are those role names and their English/Arabic labels correct for your actual organization? Define any missing role by its duties rather than its title alone.
Who establishes a diocese and appoints its first bishop in the intended onboarding process? The current appointment policy does not expose bishop appointment as an ordinary assign-access option.
What information and approvals are required to create a parish, and when should it become publicly visible and operational?
Can a parish have multiple priests, secretaries, treasurers and administrators, and does each group need a designated lead?
When one account has several roles in one parish, should permissions combine automatically, or should the user explicitly enter a role/workspace?
When roles differ between parishes, what must the header and action confirmations show to make the active authority unmistakable?
Approve a matrix for viewing, creating, editing, approving, signing, releasing, exporting and archiving each record type. Where must administrative authority stop short of clergy authority?
Which exact office duties may Parish Admins and higher administrators perform when there is no secretary? Guest document controls need to agree with this policy.
Which duties may a priest delegate, to whom, for what period and with what visible notice? Which actions must remain personal to that priest?
When someone is absent, transferred, retired, suspended or deceased, who handles their pending approvals and assigned work?
What should happen to open forms and pending actions when access is revoked during a session? What explanation and safe destination should the user receive?
Should appointments have start/end dates, invitation acceptance or periodic review? What should upcoming expiry look like to the appointee and administrator?
Which administrative changes need a reason, a second approver or current-password confirmation, and how should the confirmation describe its exact effect?
How should a user request missing access or challenge an incorrect appointment without seeing unauthorized records or other people's account details?
What should be the first screen after login for each role, including an account with no parish, a follower without membership and an unassigned priest?
Should staff enter their work tools and personal parish life through one switch, separate destinations, or one combined home? Confirm the current exclusion of secretary personal member routes.
Which sections should appear in each role's main navigation, and which should be reachable only from a related record or a More menu?
Which labels need changing to match users' language: People/Parishioners, Groups/Ministries, Member portal/Website content, Eparchy/Archdiocese, Services & Activities, or others?
What should the parish selector show: assigned parishes, followed parishes, all accessible parishes, primary parish and/or a combined view?
What should persist after switching parish or workspace: current page, filters, selected date, open draft and last-used view? What must reset?
For each dashboard, choose the information and actions that deserve the first visible screen. Which numbers need definitions, date periods and drill-down destinations?
Should actionable work appear in one personal queue across request types, or in separate role/module queues? Distinguish “needs me,” “needs office,” and “waiting on applicant.”
What exactly should each navigation badge count? Resolve whether it includes guest requests, membership, corrections, waitlists, bishop review and work someone else must perform.
What should global search find for each role, and which fields may results expose? Include names in either script, phone, household, request reference, register number and pages/actions.
What should selecting a search result open: a page, drawer or relevant tab? How should users return to the same result position and filters?
Which tables need saved filters, sort, column choices, page-size choices, bulk actions and selected-versus-all-matching selection?
On a phone, which actions and fields must remain immediately visible when desktop tables become cards or hide columns? Which tasks need a dedicated full-screen flow?
When a direct link points to a moved, archived, removed or unauthorized record, what should the user see and where should they be able to go next?
What is the public homepage's main job: finding a parish, finding Mass times, making a request, or explaining ParishLife? Rank the primary actions.
Which directory filters and sort choices are essential, and should visitors find Masses by day, time and language across parishes rather than only opening parish profiles?
Which details must a parish card show before a visitor opens it, including office availability or whether online requests are accepted?
Is the map preview useful at launch, or should it be hidden until a live map is available? What must happen when location access is refused or coordinates are missing?
What must every parish profile contain, and in what order should story, visiting information, times, clergy, ministries, events, requests, updates and contacts appear?
Should missing parish information be hidden, shown as awaiting publication, or replaced with a specific contact action? Which missing fields should prevent publication?
Should illustrative photographs remain on named parish pages until verified parish images exist? Approve the wording and placement of the illustration label.
Which clergy/leader names and contact details may be public, and who confirms their publication? Should contact always route through the parish office?
Should public calendar titles include family names for baptisms, weddings and funerals? Define default visibility and who authorizes exceptions.
Which guest request types should be discoverable from parish pages? The public form also contains appointment and ministry options beyond the main request cards.
Should urgent needs such as a funeral or sick visit offer a clearly visible office/emergency contact route alongside online submission? Who maintains that contact and its availability?
What should shareable parish/event URLs, visitor language choice and return-to-results behavior preserve? Should the separate landing/marketing page remain part of the product?
Who may edit public content, who may publish it, and should clergy or another reviewer approve particular types before publication?
Should public profile details and website sections be managed together, or should their different ownership remain visible as separate editors?
When editing published content, should Save draft retain the currently published version? Confirm or replace the current behavior that unpublishes a section.
Which publishing states are needed: draft, awaiting approval, scheduled, published, expired, returned and archived? Who moves between them?
Is publishing allowed with only one language complete? If so, what should visitors and editors see when the other translation is missing?
Must editors preview the exact public page on phone and desktop before publishing, including language fallback and private/public visibility?
Which content should support rich text, links, files, galleries and captions? Who provides image descriptions and confirms permission to use photographs of people?
Should Mass/confession/office times be structured schedules with exceptions or free text? Who keeps holiday changes consistent with the calendar?
Do announcements need pinning, expiry, categories, audiences, attachments and scheduled publication? Which should appear on both public and member pages?
Should each parish be allowed to change public branding/layout, or should the current shared public theme remain uniform while dashboard colors stay personal?
What should happen when two editors change the same section: compare versions, keep a recoverable draft, request refresh, or assign an editor lock?
Who can see publication history, revert a mistake and remove an accidentally published private item? What should be retained in the audit record?
Confirm who may create their own account and the minimum age. What is the intended account model for younger children and adults who cannot manage their own login?
Which signup fields are essential immediately, and should Arabic name, address, parish and other profile details remain for later?
Should new users sign in primarily with email, phone or username? Is selecting the identifier type desirable, or should one field recognize it with clear errors?
How should signup explain a phone/email already in use, shared family contacts and possible existing office records without exposing another person's account?
Must a contact be verified before login, submitting a request, linking a parish record or holding a staff role? What happens when verification is unavailable or a code does not arrive?
Which external sign-in providers and MFA, if any, belong in launch? Until then should unavailable provider buttons be hidden or visibly disabled with an explanation?
What password guidance, visibility toggle, password-manager behavior and validation feedback should members and staff receive? Should the experience differ by privilege?
What should Forgot password do for a member, a privileged staff account and an account with no usable verified contact? Define identity review and who may help.
Should office-created people receive invitations, through which real channel, and what should the recipient see before accepting the person link?
Confirm the invitation expiry and one-use rule. What should expired, already-used, revoked and wrong-person invitations offer as a recovery action?
How may a user change or remove a login email/phone, recover a lost device, sign out other devices and detect an unfamiliar session?
What should login rate limiting, disabled accounts, session expiry and shared-computer sign-out communicate? What draft work should survive reauthentication?
What can a follower see/do before parish membership is approved, and what should explain the benefit and meaning of formal membership?
Can someone be a full member of several parishes simultaneously, and does primary parish affect eligibility, notifications, records or only defaults?
What evidence must the office check to approve a membership link, and how should it document verification without keeping unnecessary private evidence?
When no matching person exists, should membership review allow creating one inside the review flow rather than leaving the queue and returning later?
How should the office compare several possible person matches, detect an existing account link and correct a link made to the wrong person?
When membership is declined, should a reason be required and visible to the applicant? Can they correct information and reapply?
How can a member leave a parish, unfollow it or change primary parish, and what happens to active requests, group roles and historic records?
Should existing person invitations bypass any membership steps, or must the office approve every claim? What does an already signed-in recipient experience?
Which official fields may a person propose correcting, and which require office-only handling or documentary proof?
Should a correction be approved as one proposal or field by field? Can the office modify the proposed value, and must the applicant accept that change?
While a correction waits, may the applicant withdraw or replace it? How should a staff edit to the same field be compared and resolved?
How should My account, My profile and My parish records explain which information controls login, personal display, office contact and official certificates?
Which categories of person belong in People: parishioners, visitors, children, nonmembers, non-Catholic spouses, clergy, deceased people and outside witnesses? Define their statuses.
What is the minimum information needed to save a person? Should a record be allowed when the Arabic/English name, birth date, phone or address is unknown?

What name structure is needed for daily work and official documents: given/family names, parents' names, birth surname and title? Confirm that automatic transliteration and Preferred Name remain excluded.
How should approximate/unknown dates, people without phones and international contacts be entered? Should Lebanese phone formatting ever reject an overseas person?
Which address choices must be selectable, and what is the path for a town, sector or foreign address absent from the verified list?
Is collecting blood type, medical/allergy information, skills and occupation necessary? For each, specify the purpose, permitted viewers and visibility in ordinary profiles.
What must appear in the profile header and default tab, and which of Family, Groups, Sacraments, Attendance, Giving, Activity, Notes, Files and Consent should each role receive?
When staff add someone to a group from a person form/profile, should this take immediate effect or go through leader/priest approval? Reconcile this with member-initiated applications.
Which edits need a reason, supporting document or approval, and which fields become locked after use in an official entry?
What photo capture/crop/replace/remove experience is required, including consent, missing images and a recognizable fallback?
Which contact and directory consent choices are needed, what exact information do they cover, and who may record or withdraw consent on another person's behalf?
When opening a profile, which related actions should be available directly: message, invitation, new request, certificate, registration, household edit or private note? Specify role restrictions.
What defines a household for your parish: shared residence, family relationship, shared finances or another rule? How should extended families at different addresses be represented?
Is one current household per person sufficient for separated parents, shared custody, students away from home and members living abroad?
Is “household head” the right label, or should the interface use household contact? What authority, if any, does that designation confer?
Which relationships must be represented, including step/adoptive parents, guardians, deceased relatives, siblings and unrelated residents? Which should remain private?
How should users enter a relationship to a specific person and resolve missing, conflicting or circular relationships in the family diagram?
When changing the household head/contact, should all relationships remain as currently documented, and what comparison should be shown before saving?
Which address/contact fields are shared, and how should individual overrides and a household move affect each member's record?
Can any household adult request a sacrament or certificate for another adult, or is explicit authorization needed? Household membership alone may not establish permission.
What must a guardian see/manage for a child, and when should the child's own account take over those responsibilities?
How should joining, splitting, merging or leaving households preserve previous relationships, consent, giving and open requests?
Confirm the optional household envelope identifier: who assigns it, how uniqueness is checked, and what happens when the household splits or the identifier changes?
What should household cards, the diagram, printed directory and selected/filtered exports include? Should restricted relationships or nonconsenting members be omitted from each?
Which records must be brought in before launch, from which real formats and with what approximate volume? Include paper registers and previous spreadsheets if applicable.
Who maps source columns, previews data, confirms import and resolves invalid rows? Should a partially valid file be imported in parts or rejected as a whole?
How should import handle missing translations, unsupported localities, inconsistent dates, phone formats and consent that is absent or undocumented?
What identifies a likely duplicate, and which facts should reviewers compare before concluding two records represent the same person?
Who may merge records, and how should the UI resolve conflicting fields, household/group links, account links, sacramental entries and financial history?
Must an incorrect merge be reversible? What should the pre-merge impact summary and subsequent history contain?
Which person statuses require archiving rather than ordinary editing, and what should happen to accounts, rosters, pending requests and scheduled reminders?
How can a permitted user find and restore archived people while avoiding duplicate recreation during signup, membership or child-request review?
What should happen when someone relocates to another parish, given that the transfer workflow was removed? Confirm the intended office procedure and record visibility.
How should historical sacraments entered after the fact differ from newly celebrated ones, including source evidence, original dates, celebrants and register numbering?
Which legacy items need a visible “requires review/linking” state before use, such as unlinked event forms or older certificates? Who completes that work?
What migration preview, reconciliation totals and approval are required before staff trust imported/historical data as official?
Which request types should exist at launch, and which should be structured forms versus a general “Ask the parish” request? Include appointments, ministry inquiries, Mass intentions and visits.
Should guests and linked members provide the same core information for the same service? If guest intake stays simpler, who obtains the missing details and where are they entered?
Can an unlinked account submit through its account rather than returning to the public guest form? What advantages or restrictions should that account receive?
Who may submit for someone else, and how should relationship/authorization be confirmed? Include children outside the household, another adult, a deceased relative and an overseas requester.
Should office staff enter telephone/in-person requests into the same intake flow, identifying their origin and requester, or create the office record directly?
What should submission show before the final action: parish, subject, required documents, expected review time, fees, privacy and a reviewable summary?
Should all request types share one reference, timeline and conversation from intake to completion, including guest-to-office conversion, or should linked references remain visible?
What office triage information is needed: urgency, deadline, assigned person, missing information, last contact and current next action? Who may change each?
How should the office request more information without declining the request? Can applicants edit fields, add documents or reply while it waits?
What distinguishes received, accepted for processing, clergy-approved, scheduled, completed and ready for collection in the applicant's language?
Until which stage can applicants edit or withdraw a request? After acceptance, should they request cancellation/rescheduling, contact the office, or perform a direct action?
Which decisions require applicant-visible reasons, and how should internal staff notes be visually separated so they cannot be accidentally sent?
How should duplicate submissions, wrong-parish requests and an office acceptance made in error be handled without losing the request history?
What should the guest success/tracking page show, and how can a guest recover a lost link, revoke a leaked link, receive updates and later link the request to an account?
Who owns overdue or unattended requests, what review times can the interface honestly promise, and how should applicants and staff escalate a delay?
Confirm the exact lifecycle for each sacrament, including whether office review is optional and whether a priest can bypass it without a separate explanation.
What should priest acceptance mean operationally: permission to start preparation, eligibility confirmed, date reserved, or a different commitment?
Which preparation requirements are mandatory, which are optional, and who may configure or waive them? What should a waiver record and display?
Must all required preparation be complete before selecting a date, before marking Scheduled, or only before celebration? Distinguish a tentative date from a confirmed date.
Should date, time, church/room, celebrant and relevant family availability be checked together against calendar and clergy conflicts? Who can authorize an exception?
How should a group celebration containing several people be entered, prepared and approved while preserving separate individual official entries?
Who confirms that a celebration occurred, what facts must be checked, and what should happen for a no-show, changed celebrant or changed celebration time?
What must a priest compare before approving an official entry, and can they return it for correction instead of rejecting the underlying request?
Define official numbering: scope by parish/sacrament/year/book, when allocated, treatment of gaps, historical numbering and whether it may ever be changed.

If an approved official entry contains an error, what is the authorized correction process? Confirm whether an in-app correction flow should return or remain an office procedure outside the current UI.
How should cancellation, rejection and reopening work at each stage, especially after celebration or official registration? Which actions must be impossible?
Approve the numbered progress timeline: finished/current/future steps, timestamps, waiting duration, planned date, responsible person/role and what each audience may see.
Should Requests remain the main way to find official entries, or is a dedicated searchable register needed? Decide how book/page/year searches and complete register exports should work.
For baptism, which child/adult, birth, parent, guardian, godparent, address and eligibility details are required at intake, preparation and official entry respectively?
When a baptism concerns an unregistered child, who may create/match their person record and choose the household? What should happen if an archived or ambiguous match exists?
For adult baptism or a person with incomplete parental information, which fields and preparation differ, and how should the form avoid impossible required fields?
For First Communion, what prior records, age/formation evidence and group preparation must be checked? Can applicants provide evidence from another parish?
How should confirmation/chrismation vary by rite and its relationship to baptism? Which terminology, separate records and request options should be shown?
For marriage, what information is required for both partners, their parishes, witnesses, prior records and preparation? Can one partner be outside the local people database?
Which marriage cases need a different approval route or outside authorization, and how should the UI identify that need without making the decision itself?
For funerals, what deceased-person, family-contact, celebrant, location and timing information is essential, and which steps must support urgent handling?
Should completing a funeral automatically mark a person deceased, or require a separate reviewed update? What should stop future invitations, commitments and inappropriate reminders?
For Mass intentions, blessings, sick visits and appointments, which details should be structured, who receives them and what event/task should acceptance create?
How should sacramental records from another parish or country be referenced and verified without treating an uploaded document as a new local celebration?
Which requirements and official labels may vary by parish/diocese/rite, and who approves those variations before they affect forms or documents?
Which fees, suggested offerings, exemptions or collection instructions apply to these requests, if any? Where should users see them without implying that payment establishes approval?
Which certificate types are required, and who will provide approved examples of their exact wording, layout, seal, signatures and required fields?
Who may request each certificate and for what purposes? What authorization is needed when requester and subject differ?
Confirm whether every newly signed certificate needs bishop acceptance, or only specified types/parishes/cases. Who has authority to approve that policy?
Approve the visible statuses before and after priest signature, bishop review, return, resubmission, acceptance, release and collection. At what point may the UI say “issued” or “ready”?
Where should a bishop find the review queue, what information/document preview must it contain, and are individual or bulk decisions permitted?
When the bishop returns a certificate, who sees the reason, what can the priest edit, and what must a resubmission explain? Should the applicant see this loop or only a neutral progress message?
How should the process continue during bishop/priest absence or reassignment? Are delegated signatures or acceptance ever allowed?
Can a certificate request wait on a planned sacrament, and how should automatic source linking, cancellation of the sacrament and several possible source entries be explained?
Which languages and name spellings may the requester choose, and who verifies translations? Resolve the current trilingual option against actual supported document templates.

What makes a downloaded or printed certificate official: wet signature, electronic signature, seal, serial, verification URL/QR, or an explicitly nonofficial copy? Which launch formats should be available?
Are certificates valid indefinitely or time-limited, and can copies be reprinted, replaced, revoked or corrected? What should distinguish a replacement from a new issuance?
How should preexisting issued certificates be labeled and used when they lack the new bishop-review metadata? Is any retrospective review required?
What must be verified at physical collection or secure download, including a representative collecting on someone's behalf? Who records receipt and when is the request complete?
Should certificate requests support copy quantities, fees, payment status and delivery choice? What happens when payment or pickup remains outstanding after acceptance?
For every request/preparation type, list required documents, optional evidence, who supplies each and the stage at which it becomes mandatory.
Should applicants upload documents during submission, later from tracking, or only through the office? What should a guest who cannot upload be told to bring?
What should distinguish file attached, paper received, verified, rejected/illegible, expired and waived? Is a receipt checkbox sufficient, or is verification a separate action?
Which file types, size limits, number of files and page counts are appropriate for each surface? Confirm or change the current 1 MB member versus 10 MB office difference.
Should phone users be able to photograph, rotate, crop, combine or compress documents? What preview must they see before sending?
How should uploads show progress, cancellation, retry, unsupported type, oversized file and an interrupted connection without losing the rest of the form?
Who may view, replace, download or remove a file, and must replacement retain the old version and a reason? What happens once a record is approved or closed?
Should a document be reusable across related requests, or copied/linked only after review? How should staff tell whether a reused document is still valid?
What must the release confirmation show to prevent sending the wrong person's document? Must it compare applicant, subject, certificate, file preview and intended access method?
Can a released file be withdrawn, replaced or given an expiry? What should existing guest links and previously downloaded copies mean after withdrawal?
What should the private tracking link itself reveal, should download require an additional verification step, and how should a leaked link be replaced?
What file-view/release/download activity should be visible to staff and applicants, and what retention/deletion behavior applies when the parent request is cancelled or archived?
Which calendar event types exist, and which fields, icons, colors and default audiences distinguish Mass, sacrament, group meeting, parish activity and facility block?
Which role may create/edit each event type, and who may publish an event publicly or invite a group?
What should each audience see about a private event occupying a shared room/time: hidden entirely, busy interval, or limited title/location?
Should recurring events support exceptions, cancellations and edits to one occurrence versus the series? How should changes affect bookings, registrations and volunteer assignments?
What should happen when a room, priest, leader or required equipment is double-booked? Which conflicts block saving and which require a reason to override?
When a sacrament, group meeting or service plan is dated elsewhere, should its calendar entry be created automatically? Which screen becomes the authoritative editor?
Which calendar views and filters are needed for each audience, and what should the default view, week start and displayed hours be on phone versus desktop?
Should parish times always display in the parish's time zone for overseas users, with an optional local equivalent? How should daylight-saving changes and cross-midnight events be labeled?
Are 30-minute increments and the current facility hours sufficient, or do offices need precise, early, late or all-day scheduling?
What must Print my schedule and Priest schedule include, omit and distinguish? May users export calendars or subscribe from their calendar app?
Which feasts/liturgical calendars are supported, who approves their source and corrections, and should parish exceptions be possible?
Which anniversaries should be shown to whom, how far ahead, and with what outreach action? What should happen for deceased people, private records and incomplete historic dates?
When an event is changed or cancelled, which connected workflows must be updated and which participants need to explicitly acknowledge the change?
What is a “service” versus a calendar event, sacrament request and ministry meeting in your users' vocabulary? Which should share one detail page?
Who creates a plan, who edits it, who approves it and who may see it during the activity? Can different teams collaborate on one plan?
Which plan information is mandatory: linked event, start/end, celebrant, room, team, participants, notes, readings and music?
How should an order-of-service item specify start time, duration, person responsible and instructions? Should later times recalculate when an item changes?
What should users see when the plan exceeds available time, has an unassigned role or conflicts with a related event?
Which draft, saved, approved and completed states are needed, and what should happen when someone navigates away with an unsaved plan?
Which parts of a template are copied, and which dates/people/rooms must be reviewed before reuse? Who can change a template already used by saved plans?
Which outputs are required: clergy running sheet, volunteer assignments, printable program, musician setlist and participant version? Define private instructions excluded from each.
Who owns the music library, and which metadata and search filters are needed for language, rite, season, key, instrumentation and usage rights?
How should lyrics, chords, instrument notes, audio/video links and versions be reviewed, corrected and linked to a plan without altering past plans unexpectedly?
Which music files or text may be downloaded, printed or projected, and who records the necessary permissions and attribution?
If music/planning is deferred, which existing plans and resources must remain readable and what should replace their navigation/actions at launch?
Are Groups and Ministries interchangeable in your parish, or do you need types such as committee, catechism class, choir and temporary event team?
Who creates a group, assigns its leader/co-leaders, configures eligibility and approves its public listing?
What must a prospective member see before applying: purpose, age range, schedule, location, leader contact, capacity, prerequisites and commitment expectations?
Can followers apply before formal parish membership, or must they first be linked to a person? What should the blocked application offer as a next step?
Confirm leader review followed by priest approval and the priest's direct-approval option. Are interviews, trial membership, guardian approval or group capacity decisions required?
Can staff add a person directly to a roster, and under which authority? Must that person consent or receive an invitation before being treated as active?
What should happen when a leader declines, is unavailable or has a conflict of interest? Who sees the reason, and can the applicant appeal or reapply?
Confirm the private leave process. Does membership remain active while departure waits, and can the member stop attendance/notifications immediately?
After a departure is approved, what neutral information may leaders see, and how are future meetings, assignments, resources and attendance access affected?
What is the withdrawal rule before versus after leader approval, and what should the applicant see while withdrawal itself awaits approval?
How should leadership handover, group merge/split and group closure preserve members, pending applications, files, tasks and history?
What should each role see on a group page? Confirm the secretary's smaller Members & contacts / Meetings / Resources workspace and any needed additions.
Does creating/editing a group meeting also create/update the calendar event, or should meetings and calendar events remain separate with an explicit link?
Which meeting information and materials should members receive, and when should it become visible to new or trial members?
Are RSVPs required, optional or inappropriate for some groups? Who can see absence reasons, and what is the deadline for changing a reply?
Which attendance states are needed: present, late, absent, excused, unknown and not expected? Should unrecorded attendance ever count as absence?
Who records/corrects attendance, for how long after a meeting, and what evidence/reason/history is needed for changes?
How should guests, newcomers, a participant joining midterm and former members appear in attendance sheets and summary calculations?
What is the required attendance-import flow, including template, matching, date mapping, preview, invalid rows, duplicates and reversal of a wrong import?
Which attendance figures should members, leaders, priests and bishops see, and what date range/denominator must each percentage explain?
What does Formation mean for each group: courses, milestones, eligibility, completion or certificates? Who records evidence and signs off completion?
Which resources are digital learning materials versus physical group belongings, and should the two use different labels and screens?
How should resource access, loans, returns, missing items and ownership transfer behave when a member leaves or a leader changes?
Which group tasks/notes are collaborative, which are private, and how should they remain distinct from personal member notes and confidential pastoral notes?
What makes someone a volunteer in this system: a roster flag, approved commitment, event assignment or separate reviewed volunteer record?
Can nonmembers, visitors or minors volunteer, and what consent, training or screening must be recorded before assignment?
Who defines teams, required positions, skills, dates, recurring slots and capacity for an opportunity?
Should volunteers offer availability themselves, receive assignments, sign up for open places, or use all three? Which responses need leader confirmation?
What should distinguish invited, offered, awaiting confirmation, confirmed, declined, cancelled and completed commitments in member and leader views?
Which conflicts should block assignment: overlapping duties, unavailable times, missing prerequisites, excessive workload or duties in another parish?
How should a volunteer decline, cancel late, request a swap or find a replacement? Who approves a replacement and receives notice?
How should drag-and-drop assignments be performed on touch screens and by keyboard, with a clear non-drag alternative?
Who records and approves actual hours, corrections and no-shows, and what purpose do the reports serve?
How should sign-up sheets be shared publicly or privately, how much volunteer identity/contact information may they reveal, and what should remain available after an opportunity ends?
Which activities use registration, and is one form per event sufficient? Do programs spanning several dates need session-by-session registration or one enrollment?
Who may build/open/close a form, and can creating the form also create its calendar event and reserve the room?
Should guests and members register themselves or family members online, or is registration initially office-managed? How is an unrecorded participant added safely?
What fields may the form builder offer, including conditional fields and attachments, and what should its applicant preview and validation show?
What should count toward capacity: reserved places, confirmed participants, pending approvals or a temporarily held checkout? Can staff override capacity with a reason?
What should a waitlist do when a place opens: automatic promotion, timed invitation or staff review? Who decides priority and how is expiry explained?
Confirm that reserved places may wait for consent, while final confirmation/check-in require applicable consent. Does payment ever become a separate prerequisite for confirmation?
Which consent is event-specific versus reusable, whose signature/confirmation is required, and how are missing birth date, changing age and withdrawn consent handled?
What transport options, seats, routes, pickup points, fees and deadlines are needed? What should happen when transport changes after money has been recorded?
Are fees per person, household, event or selection? Define discounts, scholarships, waived fees, installment payments and who may approve adjustments.
Which real payment methods are accepted at launch, who records receipt, and what proof/receipt should the payer receive? Keep recorded bank/OMT/cash separate from a future payment gateway.
Can payment be received in a different currency, exceed the balance, cover several participants or be recorded by someone other than the participant? Define the allocation and review experience.
How should payments be corrected or reversed while preserving history, and what links should exist to Finance without recording the same money twice?
What happens when a participant/event is cancelled: place release, waitlist action, transport adjustment, fee policy, refund approval and applicant-visible explanation?
Which form details may change after registrations begin, and how should event moves, currency changes or revised consent wording be handled when the current form is locked?
What should staff and applicants see for legacy unlinked forms, duplicate participants, closed registration, unpaid balances and registration confirmation that has not actually been delivered?
Which events and participants require check-in, and who will operate it on which devices at the door?
What identifies a participant: name search, registration reference, QR/code, household lookup or printed list? Which fallback is required?
Can a walk-in register and check in immediately, and how should staff resolve full capacity, missing consent, unknown age and unpaid fees?
Which alerts must appear before check-in, and who may see medical, allergy, guardian or pickup restrictions without exposing them to bystanders?
How should duplicate arrival, wrong-event selection, checkout/reentry and corrections to an arrival time be handled?
Who defines authorized collectors, verifies their identity and records pickup restrictions? Is the authorization global, event-specific or both?
How is a pickup code issued, delivered, replaced if lost and checked? Is a matching code alone sufficient, or must staff also verify the collector?
What must happen when an unauthorized or restricted person arrives, a guardian cannot be reached, or staff need to record an exception? Name the real decision owner and escalation route.
When a participant can leave independently, who records that permission and what checkout evidence is needed?
Should incident reports link to event, person and location while remaining accessible only to authorized staff? Which information should guardians or other participants receive?
What incident lifecycle is required: initial record, immediate response, assigned reviewer, follow-up, notifications, resolution and restricted amendments?
What should an emergency roster include and explicitly exclude? If you need everyone in a building, what additional attendance process would provide that information?
During a connection failure, what exact check-in/pickup fallback should staff follow, and how should paper/offline records be reconciled later?
What wording and training must make clear which emergency functions actually work at launch, especially since emergency broadcast delivery is not connected?
Which bookable resources exist: rooms, halls, outdoor areas, entire buildings, equipment or combinations? Which properties affect availability and eligibility?
Who can see availability and request each resource: public guests, members, group leaders, staff and external organizations?
What should a free/busy view reveal about other reservations, and should public users see different detail from staff?
When does a request hold a slot: submission, office acceptance, priest confirmation or deposit? Define hold duration and what actually ends an expired hold.
If two requests compete, should accepting one automatically refuse the other, move it to a waitlist, or ask staff to propose alternatives? Confirm the message and consent before this side effect.
What are the approval stages by resource/requester/purpose, and can office administrators confirm routine bookings without a priest?
How should setup, cleanup, opening hours, multi-day bookings, recurring use and partial-room combinations affect conflicts?
Should creating a reservation also create a calendar event, service plan or registration form? Which record owns date/time changes?
What booking details and documents are required, including purpose, guests, responsible adult, equipment, access arrangements, insurance/agreements if your parish requires them?
How should pricing, deposits, waivers, balance due and refunds work, and where should these payments appear without duplication in Finance?
Can applicants reschedule or cancel confirmed bookings, and how should fees, competing holds, room staff and linked events be updated?
When maintenance blocks a room with existing bookings, must the system prevent it, require a relocation plan, or notify affected applicants after a reviewed decision?
How should equipment quantity, condition, storage, reservations, check-out, due date, return and damage/loss be recorded? Can a room booking reserve equipment atomically?
Who can report/triage an issue, assign repair, mark a resource unusable and restore it? What evidence, costs and notification close the issue?
What information should external renter records contain, who may view it, and how do a guest requester and an external renter become the same recognized customer if appropriate?
Which availability/reservation metrics are actually useful, how are they calculated and what should display when there is not enough recorded data for a reliable figure?
Which kinds of giving must be recorded, and which are anonymous, household-attributed, person-attributed, restricted or linked to an appeal?
Who may see donor identity and amounts in lists, profiles, reports and exports? Should priests, administrators, leaders and financial viewers see different detail?
How should an envelope number find a household, and what should happen for unknown, changed, duplicated or blank envelope identifiers?
What information must a contribution capture: actual currency/amount, received date, fund, campaign, donor/household, method, reference and anonymity choice?
Confirm that a gift received in LBP is entered and retained as its actual LBP amount. How should a user distinguish that from a displayed USD equivalent?
Who opens a counting session, what identifies its source/date and how are cash, bank and other payment totals kept separate?
What does a genuine second count involve: independent totals, line-by-line review, a second person's authenticated approval, or another procedure?
What should happen when counts disagree or a second counter is unavailable? Which exceptional actions are allowed, by whom, with what evidence?
When closing a session, which balances/records are posted, what becomes locked, and what confirmation proves completion rather than showing fixed sample success text?
How should errors after closure be reversed/corrected, including wrong donor, wrong fund, incorrect currency and cancelled bank payment?
What do pledges and standing gifts promise operationally: expected payments, reminders, allocations or actual automatic collection? Confirm launch behavior where no payment processor exists.
Who creates/ends campaigns, what should be public about progress and donors, and how should restricted or excess funds be handled in the interface?
Which contribution receipts and annual household statements are required, who reviews them and how are corrections/reissues recorded? What wording confirms their actual status and purpose?
Should members see their giving history or download statements, and how does household attribution affect what one household member may see?
Is ParishLife intended as the authoritative parish accounting system or an administrative ledger alongside another accounting process? What information must be exchanged with that process?
Which roles may view, enter, approve, pay, reverse, reconcile and export each financial record? Can the person submitting a payment/expense approve it?
What funds, restrictions, budgets and reporting periods are required, and who can create/change them or move money between them?
What makes an expense draft, submitted, approved, paid, rejected or reimbursed? Confirm whether amount thresholds such as those shown in current UI should actually determine approval authority.
What expense evidence is mandatory, how are missing receipts handled, and what should distinguish a supplier invoice, actual payment and a reimbursement claim?
For each transaction, which original currency, rate/date/source and converted amount must be stored and displayed? Who may override a rate and what reason must appear?
Which screens need separate currency balances versus a reporting equivalent? Define rounding and the presentation of mixed-currency totals so users cannot mistake them for actual cash.
How should bank lines enter the system, and what matching choices are needed for split/combined payments, fees, duplicates and unmatched differences?
What review confirms reconciliation, who may undo a match and what should be locked when a month/year is closed?
Should event fees, room rentals, refunds and contributions share Finance transaction references? Define the source of truth so money is counted once.
Confirm the intended separation of Office Expenses from Finance. How is an allowance transferred into the office ledger represented in overall reporting without double-counting it?
Who may enter an office opening balance, and how should duplicate/incorrect opening balances, negative balances and corrections to previous months be handled?
Should office transactions allow edit/delete as now, require reversals, or use different rules before and after monthly review? What should happen to their receipts?
Which printed vouchers, receipts, monthly summaries and exports are required, in which language/currency, and which need signatures or named approval?
Which financial reports and donor details should bishops/diocesan administrators receive: aggregates, itemized transactions, individual identities or explicitly granted subsets?
What should a finance viewer encounter when an action requires editing authority, and how should all sample/static financial claims be replaced with meaningful empty or incomplete-data states?
Which communications should be private conversations, audience announcements, public notices or group posts? Should users compose them from one entry point or different clearly named tools?
Who can message whom, including strangers in the same parish, guests, minors, leaders and people in other parishes? Which recipient details should be searchable?
What identity should a recipient see: individual sender, parish office, ministry or priest? Can staff reply on behalf of a shared office without sharing a login?
Are conversations one-to-one or may they include households, staff teams and groups? Who may join later and read earlier messages?
What are the rules for attachments, reply threads, unread state, archive, retention and recipient notification? Confirm whether sent messages remain uneditable/undeletable.
Should request discussions happen on the request timeline or in Inbox, and how should both point to the same conversation without duplicate work?
Which notices/posts need approval, pinning, expiry, translation and public/member/group audiences? How does changing a person's membership affect access to earlier content?
Who may submit prayer intentions, what should be anonymous/private/public, who approves publication and how can a person withdraw a sensitive intention?
Which real external channels are essential at launch? For each unavailable channel, should controls be hidden, disabled, or offer a clearly labeled manual handoff?
What should draft, scheduled, sent to in-app recipient, delivered externally, read, failed and cancelled mean? Which of those states can launch actually verify?
Which automated reminders or message rules are required, what triggers them and who owns the content? Should nonrunning automation records be visible as planning-only configurations?
Complete a notification row for every important transition across membership, requests, certificates, events, volunteers, payments, concerns and appointments. Which roles receive each update?
Which notifications are optional versus required operational notices, and how should channel choices, quiet hours, digests and language preferences work?
Where should notifications be read across multiple parishes, and should opening their linked record mark them read? Define badge counts, stale links and dismissed/archived updates.
How should failed delivery, duplicate recipients, changed contact details and reopened requests affect retries and status messages? Who needs to follow up manually?
How should a user report unwanted contact or an inappropriate message, and when should the existing exceptional exact-message administrative review be available and audited?
What should the feature be called so users understand its purpose, and which matters belong here versus ordinary requests, feedback or incident reporting?
Who may submit: linked members, unlinked accounts, minors and/or guests? What support route is available to someone who cannot use the portal?
Which categories and urgency choices are needed, who maintains them and which require specially authorized reviewers?
What must the submission screen say about confidentiality, anonymity to reviewers, technical limits and appropriate immediate-help routes before a person submits?
Should the submitter select reviewers as now, choose an independent office, or use automatic routing? What understandable information helps them choose safely?
What happens when every available reviewer has a conflict, the complaint involves the priest/bishop, or the selected reviewer becomes conflicted later?
Who may see case contents, counts, status, evidence and identified submitter details? Confirm that unrelated administrators receive none of these simply because of their role.
What does accepting a case assignment entail, and who may reassign/escalate it without exposing it to a broader staff queue?
Define case statuses, response deadlines, review ownership, escalation and closure/reopening rules. Which steps should the submitter see?
How should reviewer-only notes, applicant-visible replies and requests for more information be visually separated and confirmed before sending?
May an anonymous submitter later identify themselves, or an identified submitter later hide identity? What should previously authorized readers and historic evidence retain?
What evidence uploads, downloads, redactions, exports and case-history access are permitted, and which actions require an extra reason or review?
How should follow-up and outcome notifications avoid sensitive case details on shared devices, email subjects or ordinary staff dashboards?
What should happen when the submitter leaves the parish, a reviewer loses their appointment, the account closes, or a case predates automatic account tracking?
What belongs in personal member notes, confidential pastoral notes, group notes/tasks and office workflow tasks? Approve labels and boundaries that prevent accidental sharing.
Confirm whether private pastoral notes remain inaccessible to successor priests, bishops and administrators, including after the author leaves. What access should the author retain then?
When an author shares with parish priests, does that include priests appointed later? Can sharing be withdrawn, and what should prior readers and copies mean?
Can a pastoral task be assigned while its content is still author-private? What should the UI explain before assignment, and who may actually complete or edit it?
Which notes/tasks need linked people, meetings, categories, priority, due dates, recurrence, reminders and attachments? Avoid implying a reminder runs if no scheduler exists.
How should completion, reopening, deletion and archiving work for each note/task type, including what is retained in a privacy-appropriate history?
Which real office processes need the separate workflow builder beyond the hard-coded sacrament/request processes? Give a completed example for each.
Who may define a workflow, publish a form, start a run, assign a step and view its submitted answers? Should templates vary by parish or diocese?
Which workflow features are essential: sequential steps, conditional branches, parallel approvals, attachments, deadlines, return/rejection and escalation?
When a workflow definition changes, should running tasks keep the old version? What does pausing a workflow do to new submissions and existing tasks?
What should a task detail show about completed steps, timestamps, next owner and final result? When should the last step automatically close it?
How should cancelling, undoing, reopening and transferring workflow runs behave, and which notification/audit evidence must accompany those actions?
What should the administrator's main screen prioritize at system, diocese and parish scope, and how should changing management scope differ visually from changing working parish?
Should staff accounts be created by administrators with a temporary password, or invited to establish their own credentials? How should an existing ordinary account receive an appointment?
Is the current exact-username lookup suitable for appointing someone outside the visible account list? What should an administrator do when they know only the person's name or email?
How should account identity, linked parish person, clergy title and active appointments be presented separately so changing one does not imply changing the others?
Confirm the process for appointing/revoking secretaries, including several secretaries and none. What pending responsibilities should be shown before removing the last one?
How should administrators review the consequences of deactivating a parish, a parish-specific account access or a global account? Which connected users/workflows need notices and recovery routes?
What should clergy title changes and cross-parish appointments require, including the current restriction on demoting a priest to Deacon while priest assignments remain?

Which actions belong only in Administration and which in Parish settings? Should the older Roles & permissions, module toggles and security/integration screens be removed, read-only or reconciled with the actual policy?

For Presence, Office, Community and Complete, specify the actual feature matrix, record limits if any, public/member access and launch availability. Are the bundle names understandable to parish decision-makers?
Who can activate/change a parish-managed bundle, and what approval process applies when the diocese sponsors it? What should a pending plan-change request show?
Are prices, invoices, renewal dates, trials and subscriptions part of launch, or is bundle administration entirely manual? What should the public bundles page promise?
When a module is disabled or a bundle downgraded, exactly which historical records remain readable/exportable, which pending approvals can finish and which new submissions are blocked?
What should members/guests see when their parish stops accepting online requests or a feature is unavailable under its bundle? Which office fallback and tracking access remain?
What should a bishop's overview show across parishes, with what date filters, drill-down permissions and explanations of incomplete data? Is comparison/ranking between parishes appropriate?

For each existing report—attendance, membership, group participation, volunteer workload, facilities, giving, budget and registration versus attendance—what real decision does it support and how must each measure be calculated?
Which report filters, languages, date ranges, print layouts and export formats are needed, and should exports contain all matching records or only the visible page?
Who may see general versus administrative audit history, which events/fields must be included or excluded, and how should users find the reason/actor for a disputed change?

Are API credentials, webhooks, external reporting and AI assistance actual launch features? For each retained integration, who configures it and what honest configured/unavailable/error experience is required?
Which parts of the current visual design should be retained, and which concrete screens feel crowded, confusing, too formal, too plain or inconsistent? Give examples by screen name.
What visual character should the public site and staff workspace convey, and are their different current styles intentional?
Which logo, parish seal, colors, typography and icon conventions are final assets? Who approves them and can local parishes vary any of them?
Should staff screens optimize for dense office work or larger, guided interactions, and should users be able to choose a compact/comfortable density or larger text?
Which personal palette/dark-mode choices should remain, and how should custom colors be constrained so status, focus, text and errors remain readable?
When should a record open in a page, side drawer or dialog? Which complex flows need a dedicated full page, especially on phones?
Which actions deserve a primary button, which should be secondary, and which belong in a More menu? Approve a consistent placement for Save, Cancel, Back and destructive actions.
What confirmation is appropriate for approval, public publication, document release, merge, removal and cancellation? Which reversible actions should use Undo instead of interrupting dialogs?
How should forms indicate required/optional/conditional fields, explain unfamiliar terms, show progress and preserve values after validation errors?
Should errors appear beside fields, in a summary, or both, and what should receive focus? Which success messages need a persistent record/timeline rather than a temporary toast?
What should English/Arabic switching preserve: route, form draft, selected filters and scroll? Which values should display both scripts regardless of interface language?
Choose conventions for Arabic/Western digits, names, date order, month names, time format and USD/LBP formatting in screens, documents and exports separately.
Which mixed-direction fields must remain left-to-right inside Arabic screens, including phone, email, URLs, identifiers and currency? Which navigation/icons need mirroring?
Who approves bilingual terminology and error/help text? What should the interface do when a field or published content has only one translation?
Is French required at launch, later or excluded? Which currently visible unsupported language options and trilingual claims should be removed or disabled accordingly?
Which tasks must work fully by keyboard and screen reader, including calendars, family diagrams, tables, selection, drawers, uploads and volunteer scheduling? What nonvisual alternatives are needed?
What text-size/zoom, touch-target, color/contrast, reduced-motion and focus behavior must be validated with the actual intended users, especially older staff and parishioners?
For long tables and calendars on phones, which information becomes cards, expandable details or horizontally scrollable content, and what must never disappear?
Which print/download designs must work in Arabic, English and bilingual form with long names, multiple pages, missing optional data and office printers?
What should loading, first use, no records, no search results, denied access, unavailable feature and service failure look like on each main surface? Approve the next action in every state.
Which interactions should save immediately, autosave a draft or require explicit Save? Define consistent rules for records, preferences, attendance grids, plans and long request forms.
What should indicate unsaved, saving, saved, save failed and changed elsewhere, and which message must remain visible until the issue is resolved?
Should users resume drafts across refresh, logout, device change or language switch? How long may sensitive drafts persist, especially on shared computers?
When Back, Close, parish switch or sign-out would discard changes, what choices should be offered and which safe destination should follow each choice?
Which exact tasks must work without a connection: viewing already loaded pages, drafting, attendance/check-in, payment entry or none? Define each permitted offline action explicitly.
What should the user be told when an action requires a connection, and what manual fallback or recovery should be available?
If offline writes are required, how should pending changes, changed permissions, duplicates, approvals and stale availability be reviewed before synchronization?
When two users edit the same data, should the second compare field changes, refresh and reapply, or preserve a recoverable draft? Which conflicts require office review?
If a save succeeds but its response is lost, how should retry avoid creating a duplicate request, payment, check-in or approval?
If a record saves but its attachment or notification fails, what should the user see and how should they retry only the failed part?
What should happen when the active role/parish is revoked, a module changes or a linked person is archived while the user is editing?
What should timeout, unexpected server error and service maintenance messages show, including a useful reference for support without exposing internal or private data?
How should stale pages refresh when another person changes request status, room availability, check-in or a financial balance? Which actions need a fresh confirmation?
Which bulk operations need progress, preview, partial-failure results, cancellation and a downloadable outcome report? How should completed items be distinguished from retriable ones?
What should users be able to recover after accidental removal, cancellation or incorrect approval, and how long should Undo/restore be available for each record type?
What should the interface call a data snapshot versus an actual restorable backup, and who should receive the recovery/export controls for each?
For people, accounts, official registers, certificates, requests, financial evidence, incidents, concerns, notes and messages, who approves retention rules and the actions available at expiry?
How should a person request access to their information, a correction, account closure or deletion, and who reviews it when official/historical records must remain?
What should a deactivation/deletion review show about linked households, minors, active requests, giving, messages and shared records before a decision is made?
Who may export which data, how should scope/private fields be reviewed before export, and what explanation should accompany a download containing personal information?
Who handles support for members, guests, office users and administrators? Where should Help appear and what fictional/sanitized information should a support request contain?
What first-use setup should guide a new parish through identity, staff, approved requirements, public content, opening balances and legacy-data review before opening to applicants?
Which role-specific guidance, checklists, examples and training materials are needed, and which screens should link to a plain-language explanation of the procedure?
What should an administrator see before launch about unavailable integrations, incomplete translations, missing setup and legacy records that still require attention?
Which people will test the prototype as guest, member, guardian, secretary, priest, leader, treasurer, bishop and administrator? Name a responsible reviewer for each retained role.
Which real tasks will those reviewers perform without coaching, and what observable result, acceptable completion time and error tolerance determine success?
Which layouts/languages/devices must be approved, including a small phone, office desktop, Arabic right-to-left and a printed official document?
What findings block design approval, who resolves disagreements and who signs off the final prototype, permission matrix and workflow specifications?
Which unanswered decisions may be deferred, with what launch fallback? Who owns each remaining decision and what is its resolution date?
After approval, how should a changed workflow be documented, re-prototyped and reapproved before coding so screens, permissions, notifications and printed documents remain consistent?

scenarios.question: A new adult signs up, follows two parishes, chooses a primary parish, skips profile completion and returns later.
The office cannot confidently match a membership applicant to two similar person records; one is already linked to another account.
A parent requests baptism for an unregistered child; a similar archived record exists and the Arabic name is not yet known.
A guest submits the same baptism need, loses the tracking link, then creates an account and asks to associate the request.
A secretary reviews a request with missing documents; a priest accepts directly; the applicant supplies an illegible file that must be replaced.
A marriage involves a partner from another parish and an external celebrant; the planned room/priest is already busy.
A scheduled celebration is postponed, cancelled or never takes place; a certificate request was waiting on it.
The office submits a celebrated sacrament with a name error; the priest returns it; after approval another official correction is needed.
A priest signs a certificate; the bishop returns it; it is corrected, accepted and released to a verified representative.
A guest's certificate file is prepared but not released; a wrong-file release is caught or must be withdrawn after release.
A person joins a ministry, withdraws after leader review, reapplies, then later requests a private departure.
A leader changes; the former leader has open tasks, group files, attendance corrections and a pending application.
A volunteer is already assigned in another parish, accepts a new duty, then cancels shortly before the event.
An event fills while two families register; one child lacks a birth date/consent and another has a partial fee plus paid transport.
An event moves date/room after participants pay; consent/transport changes and some participants request refunds.
A child arrives, the connection fails and an unauthorized collector later asks for pickup; paper fallback is used and reconciled.
An incident occurs during one event; a restricted report is created and an emergency roster is printed without implying whole-building coverage.
Two room requests compete, one has setup time, a deposit is involved and maintenance later blocks the confirmed booking.
Equipment reserved for a paid external renter is returned damaged and becomes unavailable for another booking.
Counters record actual USD and LBP gifts, disagree, resolve the count, close it and later correct the wrong fund/household attribution.
A registration/rental payment reaches Finance while an office allowance is recorded; reporting must count each movement correctly once.
An anonymous concern names a senior cleric, selected reviewers become conflicted, and ordinary administrators must see neither the case nor its count.
A priest shares one pastoral task but keeps another note private, then leaves the parish and loses the parish appointment.
An editor changes a published bilingual page in draft, another editor publishes a concurrent change and one translation is missing.
An Archdiocese Admin creates its first parish without a secretary and delegates routine office work without granting priest signature authority.
A diocese-sponsored parish downgrades its bundle with open sacrament requests, unpaid registrations and documents awaiting release.
A user has different roles in two parishes, switches parish mid-task and receives a revocation while another tab remains open.
A financial viewer searches, prints and exports permitted records while trying an editing link from an old bookmark.
A user completes a long Arabic form using a phone or keyboard/screen reader, changes language, loses their session and resumes safely.
A deceased/archived person has a household envelope, future commitments, an account, certificates and notification preferences.
